title: Same Team
tagline: Twelve short sessions on co-parenting across two homes: one team, a shared goal, flooded means pause, businesslike messages, reliability, and the handoff ritual.
course_purpose: Twelve short film sessions on co-parenting: one team for your children, a shared goal, the flooded pause, businesslike messages, cooler channels, reliability inside every order, and a calm handoff ritual.
audience: Built for fathers raising children across two homes. Friendship with the other parent is not required. Practices stay inside the rules and orders that govern him now.
facilitator_note: Self-paced film. About twelve minutes each. Watch when you can. A Certified Facilitator is available for questions and accountability when your seat is claimed. Optional live cohorts may be offered by some programs. Logged sessions and a checkable practice. Completion never requires contact with your child, and no practice ever asks you to go beyond the rules that govern you now or any court order.

sessions.title: One Team for the Children
sessions.keyline: Whatever we are to each other, we are one team for the child.
sessions.one_scene: A parent-teacher meeting. The two adults sit one seat apart, not touching, not fighting, and both sign the same plan for the same child. The child sleeps easier that night.
sessions.in_the_room: What being on one team means when the adults may not be together, with the child's experience at the center.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can state the shared frame in child-centered terms.
sessions.practice: Write one child-centered team sentence and keep it where you will see it before hard contact.
sessions.science_or_note: A child caught between adults carries the load in his body; one shared frame lowers it.

sessions.title: Write the Shared Goal
sessions.keyline: One child-centered sentence you can both hold.
sessions.one_scene: He wants a ten-point manifesto. He writes one sentence instead: We keep school nights calm so she can sleep and learn. That sentence steers the next hard text.
sessions.in_the_room: You draft one child-centered goal sentence clear enough to hold when heat rises. Agreement on everything is not required.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You have one child-centered sentence you can both hold.
sessions.practice: Write one shared-goal sentence. Send it through a permitted channel, or file it to send when allowed.
sessions.science_or_note: One clear goal steers hard moments better than a stack of demands.

sessions.title: Flooded Means Pause
sessions.keyline: Flooded means pause. Then come back.
sessions.one_scene: The message thread heats up and he can feel his heartbeat in his ears. He names the pause, puts the phone face down, and walks. Later he comes back, and the conversation works.
sessions.in_the_room: When your heart is racing, the thinking brain goes offline. You train recognizing flood, pausing, then coming back.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can recognize flooding in yourself and pause before you make it worse.
sessions.practice: Rehearse the pause rule once. Use it on any heated exchange this week and log both ends.
sessions.science_or_note: Past a racing heartbeat nobody absorbs a word. Pause. Come back when you can think.

sessions.title: Break Clean
sessions.keyline: Break off clean. Name when you will resume.
sessions.one_scene: He almost ghosts the thread. Instead he writes: I am flooded. Let's resume at 8 tonight. At eight he shows up. The topic survives because the break was clean.
sessions.in_the_room: You practice a short break-off script that names the pause and the resume time. No speech. No slam.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can break off clean and resume when you said.
sessions.practice: Write a clean break-off line with a resume time. Use it once on a heated call or thread.
sessions.science_or_note: Naming the resume turns a pause into a trustworthy reset.

sessions.title: Businesslike
sessions.one_scene: Three lines. Pickup Friday at five. Homework due Sunday. Doctor confirmed Tuesday. Nothing about the past. The reply comes back the same way.
sessions.in_the_room: Brief, factual, child-focused communication. Where the adults are not together, the low-contact model that keeps heat out of the channel.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can send a businesslike message that carries only what the child needs.
sessions.practice: Draft three businesslike messages. Send whichever a permitted channel allows; file the rest.
sessions.science_or_note: Less adult heat in the channel lightens what the child carries.

sessions.title: Cooler Channels
sessions.keyline: Use the channel that lowers heat.
sessions.one_scene: The text thread is a furnace. He moves the logistics to a written log and saves voice for a scheduled call after a pause. The facts still move. The heat drops.
sessions.in_the_room: You choose channels on purpose. Some media raise heat before a word is read. Cooler channels protect the child from spillover.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can pick the channel that lowers heat for logistics and hard topics.
sessions.practice: Name your hottest channel and your cooler backup. Move one real logistics item to the cooler channel this week.
sessions.science_or_note: Medium matters; channel choice can prevent a fight before content does.

sessions.title: Reliability Buys Trust
sessions.one_scene: For a month he is never once late for the agreed call, never once asks for an exception. Nobody says anything. The tone in the messages changes anyway.
sessions.in_the_room: How a parent earns caregiving trust through small kept promises over time. Encouragement follows the track record.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can earn trust in steps with small reliability.
sessions.practice: Identify one small reliable act and do it consistently for a week. Log it.
sessions.science_or_note: Reliability, repeated, is what reopens the gate.

sessions.title: Never Against an Order
sessions.keyline: Never ask a child to carry an adult fight, and never against an order.
sessions.one_scene: He wants an exception. He wants the child to pass a message. He does neither. He keeps the written plan exactly. Trust grows inside the line, not against it.
sessions.in_the_room: Court orders and agreements are the floor. Trust is earned inside them, never against them. Children are never messengers for adult fights.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can operate inside any legal boundary and keep adult conflict off the child.
sessions.practice: List the rules that govern you now. Choose one small act of compliance you will keep perfectly this week. Never use the child as a messenger.
sessions.science_or_note: Trust built against an order is not trust; it is risk the child pays for.

sessions.title: What the Child Carries
sessions.keyline: The child carries the distance. Lighten the load.
sessions.one_scene: Every week the child leaves one home with a bag. He learns what is hard about the bag and fixes his end: the charger, the book, the jacket for the colder house.
sessions.in_the_room: Your child's experience of moving between two homes, the load at the transition, and the warmth that builds resilience regardless of the arrangement.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can see the transition through the child's eyes and lighten one concrete load.
sessions.practice: Ask one open question about moving between homes if contact allows, or file it. Fix one logistics friction on your side.
sessions.science_or_note: Transitions are stress points; warm, practical help lightens what the child carries.

sessions.title: Two Homes, One Child
sessions.one_scene: The houses will never match perfectly. He stops fighting for identical rules and makes his own home predictable: bedtime, homework, phone off at dinner. The child stops guessing.
sessions.in_the_room: Perfect agreement is rare. Predictable rules at your place give the child ground to stand on even when the homes differ.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can run a few clear, predictable rules the child can count on at your place.
sessions.practice: Write three predictable rules for your parenting time. Post them where you will follow them.
sessions.science_or_note: A child can adapt to two homes when each home is steady.

sessions.title: The Handoff
sessions.one_scene: Same spot, same time, a calm two-minute handoff. Within a month the child stops going quiet on the ride there. Nothing was said. The routine said it.
sessions.in_the_room: A predictable handoff carries the child's things, the practical facts, and a calm goodbye. Old disputes stay off the curb.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You can run a predictable handoff that keeps adult heat away from the child.
sessions.practice: Write your handoff checklist: place, time, items, facts, goodbye. Rehearse once.
sessions.science_or_note: The handoff is where the child feels the team most directly.

sessions.title: The Handoff Ritual
sessions.keyline: Same place, same time, same calm script.
sessions.one_scene: Bag, jacket, homework. See you Thursday at five. Same script every week. The child starts handing over the bag before anyone asks.
sessions.in_the_room: You lock a short ritual: same place, same time, same calm script. You leave with a one-page plan and a first checkpoint.
sessions.what_you_leave_with: You leave with a repeatable handoff ritual and a first checkpoint.
sessions.practice: Complete a one-page handoff ritual plan and walk it through with a cohort partner or facilitator. After return, execute one handoff to the plan and log it.
sessions.science_or_note: A predictable ritual says what words cannot at the transition.
